title: Your Phone Can See Your TV Remote's Light #science #light
description:
Your phone camera can see a light your eyes cannot. Point a TV remote at the camera and press a button: the tip lights up on screen. That's infrared light, just past red. Your eyes fade out at red, but the camera's sensor keeps going. No glow? Try the selfie camera: rear cameras often filter infrared out. Bluetooth remotes won't show it, but most TV remotes have been glowing at you all along.

More about light and colour: Why is the sky blue but sunsets red? https://youtu.be/H_61WImrwoQ

Sources
- UCL Engage, How does a remote control work on a TV? (ucl.ac.uk/engage/case-studies/2022/sep/how-does-remote-control-work-tv)
- Ken's Tech Tips, How to see the invisible infrared world using your mobile phone camera (kenstechtips.com)
- The spectrum strip in the animation is schematic

Try it: does your rear camera or your selfie camera show the glow?

Script, voice and animation are AI-produced (Claude; Kokoro voice). Every claim is checked against the sources above.
